summary:
Visitors in Nord-Est stand under the framework of Italy. The region-specific signal identified here concerns regional policy and prison practice rather than entry or documentation rules.

The Veneto Regional Council passed motion n.340 at its 178th public session in Venice on 3 July, and deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 committed the regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' observance on the last school day before Christmas, while rejecting the aims of gender-awareness content. The official regional bulletin carries the primary-source text of that motion. For a trans visitor, this records an official regional position aligned against gender-awareness education in schools.

Italy's detention practice for transgender prisoners is documented in national reporting. In January 2010 the government announced plans for one of the world's first dedicated transgender prisons at Pozzale, near Florence, converting a nearly empty medium-security women's prison into a specially equipped centre for about 30 of Italy's roughly 60 transgender prisoners, most convicted of drug or prostitution offences; gay-rights groups welcomed the space and its psychological support. Before then, and as the placement practice in 2010, transgender prisoners were held in women's prisons, where they were often segregated for their own safety. Repubblica reported in 2013 that the Pozzale project was abandoned.

A 2013 La Repubblica investigation recorded the prison administration's count of 69 transsexual prisoners across ten Italian facilities. Placement tracked legal sex: female hormones could not be prescribed to prisoners who, according to their identity card, were recorded as men; trans women were held in men's sections, while those who had already undergone sex-change surgery were assigned to women's sections. Where cells were lacking, trans prisoners were placed in isolation, described as the most inhumane means of preserving their safety. Protected sections, including the G8 section at Rebibbia in Rome and the protected section at Poggioreale in Naples, imposed limitations including on partner visits. In the 2011 Terni case the Spoleto surveillance magistrate ordered the local health authority to pay for a prisoner's hormone therapy to guarantee psychophysical integrity; the ruling was appealed and a July 2012 appellate decision followed.
tangentialFactors:
The Pozzale proposal of 2008 to 2010 would have drawn trans women from the special wing of Sollicciano in Florence; the project was shelved, so the dedicated-facility model described in 2010 was not implemented.

Regional policy in Veneto on 'Natural Family Day' and gender-awareness content sits alongside national-level court and legislative developments, indicating that official positions on gender and family vary across levels of government in Italy.
localsOnly:
For transgender residents of Veneto, deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 instituted a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' school observance on the last school day before Christmas and rejected the aims of gender-awareness content, a policy carried in the official regional bulletin.

Transgender prisoners in Italian facilities are placed according to legal sex as recorded on identity documents, which determines both housing section and eligibility for hormone therapy; protected sections at Rebibbia in Rome and Poggioreale in Naples impose limits including on partner visits. The 2011 Terni ruling, with a July 2012 appellate decision, required a local health authority to fund a prisoner's hormone therapy.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the Pozzale dedicated-prison proposal or the 2013 placement practices described in the La Repubblica investigation remain current is unresolved in the source inventory; the most recent dated evidence is from 2013.

The outcome of the July 2012 appellate decision in the Terni hormone-therapy case is not sourced here.

The date of motion n.340's 3 July session is given without a year in the source inventory; the year is unresolved.
